question: Should OpenClaw retain this grouped Claw update planner as an experimental core lifecycle and consent primitive, rather than limiting the capability to plugin-owned integrations until the RFC direction is approved?
rationale: The patch creates a new core CLI and machine-readable consent contract across agent, package, MCP, cron, and workspace ownership; reviewer feedback supports parts of the design but does not settle its permanent owner boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the experimental core slice
options.body: Approve the narrow, gated core planner direction after exact-head redaction proof is posted, keeping execution in the separately reviewed apply slice.

options.title: Confirm scope through the RFC first
options.body: Pause merge until the assigned reviewer or RFC owner explicitly confirms the core ownership and consent contract for this lifecycle surface.

options.title: Route orchestration outward
options.body: Keep only generic extension seams in core and move grouped update orchestration to a plugin or external package if core ownership is not intended.

recommendation.title: Confirm scope through the RFC first
recommendation.body: Pause merge until the assigned reviewer or RFC owner explicitly confirms the core ownership and consent contract for this lifecycle surface.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned and supplied the most detailed owner-boundary and authoritative-planning review requirements.
